extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and authors reporting observational studies (epidemiology, clinical research)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist for what to include when writing reports of observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), covering title/abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and funding transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract — study design in title/abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Indicate the study’s design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (b) Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found

rubrics_metrics.name: Background/rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description:
(a) Cohort study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe methods of follow-up
Case-control study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of case ascertainment and control selection. Give the rationale for the choice of cases and controls
Cross-sectional study—Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
(b) Cohort study—For matched studies, give matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed
Case-control study—For matched studies, give matching criteria and the number of controls per case

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables — definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources/measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias

rubrics_metrics.name: Study size
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods — overall
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
(b) Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions
(c) Explain how missing data were addressed
(d) Cohort study—If applicable, explain how loss to follow-up was addressed
Case-control study—If applicable, explain how matching of cases and controls was addressed
Cross-sectional study—If applicable, describe analytical methods taking account of sampling strategy
(e) Describe any sensitivity analyses

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — numbers at each stage
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study—eg numbers potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included in the study, completing follow-up, and analysed
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
(b) Give reasons for non-participation at each stage
(c) Consider use of a flow diagram
Note: item 13 is starred in the checklist — give information separately for cases and controls in case-control studies and, if applicable, for exposed and unexposed groups in cohort and cross-sectional studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive data — participant characteristics and missingness
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give characteristics of study participants (eg demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
(b) Indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest
(c) Cohort study—Summarise follow-up time (eg, average and total amount)
Note: item 14 is starred — give information separately for cases/controls or exposed/unexposed where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study—Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Case-control study—Report numbers in each exposure category, or summary measures of exposure
Cross-sectional study—Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures
(Note: item 15 is starred — give information separately for cases/controls or exposed/unexposed if applicable.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Main results — estimates and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (eg, 95% confidence interval). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
(b) Report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorized
(c) If relevant, consider translating estimates of relative risk into absolute risk for a meaningful time period

rubrics_metrics.name: Other analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done—eg analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key results with reference to study objectives

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability (external validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding — sources and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based
